references.text: Paul quotes directly from this text and warns the Corinthians against idolatry, referring to how the Israelites sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play.
Joshua and Moses hear the sound of the people's celebration, which is linked to the 'playing' (צחק) mentioned in verse 6.
Burnt offerings and peace offerings were also sacrificed at the covenant ceremony on Sinai, highlighting the contrast between proper and improper worship.
The same Hebrew word צחק (to play/to amuse oneself) is used here, which may carry sexual connotations in this context.
The same Hebrew root word צחק is used regarding Ishmael 'playing' with Isaac, with possible negative connotations.
The Israelites participated in idolatry that involved eating sacrificial meals dedicated to foreign gods, similar to the actions in the golden calf incident.
Moses reminds the people that they acted sinfully by making the golden calf, referring to the events described in this verse.
The psalm describes how Israel made a calf at Horeb and worshiped a cast image, a poetic retelling of this event.
A direct allusion in the New Testament that confirms and interprets the Old Testament event.
